verdict.rationale: Gecko's docs describe an AI-driven scanner that produces findings with severity, confidence, call chain and PoC (gecko-security-docs-2), implying general vulnerability-class detection including things like injection/XSS, but no docs explicitly enumerate SAST rule coverage for classes like injection/XSS. Hands-on community reports directly contradict real-world accuracy: missed a real bug that Semgrep caught (gecko-security-comm-4), returned two 100%-confidence 'vulnerabilities' that were false positives (gecko-security-comm-3), and produced an inaccurate/irrelevant finding on a test repo (gecko-security-comm-5) — concrete counter-examples to the detection claim. missing for 10: explicit rule/vulnerability-class taxonomy (CWE list including injection/XSS), independent benchmark accuracy data, and resolution of the documented false-positive/false-negative reports.
